blocks.text: South Surrey BC: Your Complete 2026 Neighbourhood & Lifestyle Guide

parts.t: Posted on
March 6, 2026
by
Jared Gibbons

If you are thinking about a move to Metro Vancouver, South Surrey is likely on your list. Families, professionals and downsizers look here for space, a range of school options, beaches and parks, and a wide mix of home types.
This guide covers what to know before you move: neighbourhoods, home prices, schools, commuting, shopping and outdoor living, all in one place.
South Surrey is the southern part of the City of Surrey. It is bordered by the ocean to the west,
White Rock
and the US border to the south, and
Langley
to the east. In the 2021 Census, South Surrey had 88,445 residents, about 16% of Surrey's population, according to the
City of Surrey's South Surrey community profile
. The area takes in planned suburban neighbourhoods, golf course communities, quiet oceanside pockets and working farms.
Within one community you can find newer construction, several school options, walkable shopping and the waterfront. That mix is why many buyers start their search with
South Surrey homes for sale
South Surrey isn't a single neighbourhood. It's a collection of distinct communities, each with its own character and price range. For a wider overview, see the
South Surrey neighbourhoods guide

Grandview Heights is one of South Surrey's newer neighbourhoods. Much of the area's recent townhome and detached construction has happened here, close to two shopping areas on 24 Avenue: The Shops at Morgan Crossing and Grandview Corners. Grandview Heights Secondary, the newest secondary school in the Surrey School District, opened here in 2021.
Grandview Surrey homes
attract young families and first-time buyers who want newer construction, modern layouts and shops close by.
Morgan Creek homes
sit in a golf course community built around Morgan Creek Golf Course, with large detached homes on generous lots.
The neighbourhood has a mature, established feel, with tree-lined streets and quiet cul-de-sacs. It's a popular choice for move-up families who want more space without leaving South Surrey.
Ocean Park
sits close to the ocean and has an older, more village-like character than the newer planned communities to the north.
Homes range from modest older ranchers to renovated detached properties. The area suits buyers who put being near the water and a quieter pace ahead of new construction.
Elgin Chantrell

and Crescent Beach sit at the upper end of the South Surrey market, with waterfront and near-waterfront homes and larger estate-style properties. For recent sale prices on a particular street, ask Jared.
South Surrey luxury homes
in this area combine privacy, natural surroundings and a strong sense of community. Crescent Beach in particular has a close-knit, cottage-by-the-sea feel.
Sunnyside
is an established family neighbourhood between South Surrey's newer developments and White Rock. It offers solid detached homes and easy access to schools, parks and shopping.
It's a natural landing spot for families relocating from other parts of Metro Vancouver who want a quiet, community-oriented neighbourhood.

Hazelmere is a semi-rural pocket near the US border and the Hazelmere Golf & Tennis Club. Properties here tend to sit on larger lots, with a mix of estate homes, acreages and hobby farm properties that appeal to buyers looking for space and privacy without leaving South Surrey.
It's an option for buyers who want a rural setting with Highway 99 and the border crossings a short drive away.

South Surrey has a wider range of prices than many buyers expect. The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board (FVREB) reports South Surrey and White Rock together as one area. Its MLS® Home Price Index benchmark prices for August 2026 were:
Detached:
$1,649,200, down 7.5% from August 2025
Townhouse:
$820,300, down 11.1% from August 2025
Apartment/condo:
$550,800, down 6.2% from August 2025
Source:
Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, MLS® Home Price Index, August 2026

. A benchmark price describes a typical home, not any particular property. Neighbourhood, lot size, age and distance to the water all move prices within South Surrey, so ask Jared for recent sales in the area you're considering.

Detached prices vary widely with the neighbourhood, lot size and proximity to the ocean. Waterfront and golf course areas such as Crescent Beach, Elgin Chantrell and Morgan Creek sit at the upper end of the market. Browse
South Surrey homes under $1.8M
or
South Surrey homes over $1.8M
For buyers looking at the top of the market,
South Surrey luxury homes
include golf course properties and waterfront estates.
Townhomes are a common way for families to buy into South Surrey. Grandview Heights has many of the area's newer townhome complexes. See current
South Surrey townhomes under $1.2M
For buyers who want newer construction with room for a family, this part of the market is worth a close look.
South Surrey condos
are found mainly in Grandview Heights and along the King George Boulevard corridor. Prices depend on size, building and proximity to amenities.
Condos attract downsizers, investors and first-time buyers. Many condo buyers also look at
White Rock homes for sale
, since the two areas sit side by side.
School options are one of the main reasons families choose South Surrey. Catchments can change from one street to the next, so confirm any address with Surrey Schools before you buy. The
South Surrey schools and catchments guide
is a good place to start.

Sunnyside Elementary (K–7) and Grandview Heights Secondary serve the newer family neighbourhoods. Grandview Heights Secondary opened in September 2021 and is the newest secondary school in the district, according to its
Surrey Schools fact sheet
Semiahmoo Secondary is one of two Surrey schools that offer the full International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme. The other is Johnston Heights Secondary. The
IB Diploma is a district program of choice
, so students apply for a spot, usually in Grade 10.
Southridge School
is a K–12 independent day school on a 17-acre campus in South Surrey.
South Surrey is not a short commute to downtown Vancouver, but many residents make it work by car or by transit.
Highway 99 is the main driving route north to Richmond and Vancouver. Drive times vary a lot with traffic, so test your route at your usual commute time before you buy.
The
351 bus

runs from White Rock Centre through South Surrey to the South Surrey Park & Ride, then north on Highway 99 to Bridgeport Station on the Canada Line in Richmond. The 321 runs north along King George Boulevard from White Rock Centre through Newton to King George and Surrey Central stations on the Expo Line.
The
South Surrey Park & Ride
at 3800 King George Boulevard has 840 parking spaces for commuters who drive part of the way. Check TransLink for current schedules.
South Surrey has plenty of everyday shopping for a suburban community.

On 24 Avenue, The Shops at Morgan Crossing is an open-air shopping village with shops, a gym and a bank, and Grandview Corners at 160 Street adds large stores such as Walmart, The Home Depot and Best Buy. If you'd like to live within walking distance, see
Morgan Crossing homes for sale
and
Grandview Corners condos and townhomes
. Semiahmoo Shopping Centre, at 152 Street and 16 Avenue, serves the White Rock side of South Surrey.
The
White Rock
area adds the restaurants along Marine Drive and the White Rock Pier promenade, which many South Surrey residents treat as their own backyard.
South Surrey has a wide variety of outdoor space, from beaches to forest trails.
Crescent Beach and nearby White Rock Beach are the two main oceanfront destinations, popular with locals year-round.
Blackie Spit Park
in Crescent Beach reaches into Mud Bay at the mouth of the Nicomekl River. It's a favourite spot for walking and birdwatching, with views of Mud Bay and the North Shore Mountains.
Elgin Heritage Park
sits along the tidal Nicomekl River, with more than 3 km of nature trail, wetlands and the Historic Stewart Farm.
Redwood Park

, at 17900 20 Avenue, is home to a grove of mature Sierra redwoods. Twin brothers Peter and David Brown planted the park's forest with trees from around the world after their father gave them the land in 1893, according to the City of Surrey. Today the park has more than 5 km of trails, a replica of the brothers' treehouse and picnic shelters, and it's free to visit from dawn to dusk.
South Surrey

combines school options, beaches and parks, shopping and a wide range of housing in one community. Whether you're a growing family, a professional relocating from Vancouver or a downsizer, it deserves serious consideration.

Jared Gibbons is a REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty who specializes in South Surrey and the surrounding communities. If you're thinking about making the move, the best first step is a conversation.
